title: Anthony of the desert (c. 251–356)
hookLine: hearing the gospel of the rich young man, he sells everything and goes into the desert

cards: A young man in Egypt is walking to church. His parents have died. He's been left land, and a younger sister to look after.

He's thinking about the apostles, who left everything to follow Jesus, and the believers in Acts, who sold what they had and laid the money at the apostles' feet. He walks in just as the Gospel is being read.
It's the story of the rich young man. His name is Anthony, and what he does next starts something.

teach.b: Here's the line he heard, in the Douay-Rheims: "If thou wilt be perfect, go sell what thou hast, and give to the poor." In the Gospel, the rich young man goes away sad.
Anthony's biographer, Saint Athanasius, says Anthony heard it as if it had been read for him alone. So he did what the young man couldn't.
He gave his family's land to the people of his village, sold the rest and gave the money to the poor, keeping a little back for his sister.

Then, the story goes, he walked into church another day and heard Jesus say not to be anxious about tomorrow. So he gave away the rest, and placed his sister with a community of women who had given their lives to God.

Next, the desert. He didn't vanish all at once. Athanasius says he first learned from an old man near his village, copying the good habits of people around him: one in prayer, another in kindness, another in fasting.

Then he went farther out, to tombs, to an empty fort, and at last into the mountains, praying, working with his hands, and struggling, in Athanasius's telling, against temptations that came at him like enemies.
Then the strange part. He went to be alone, and people followed him, for advice, for healing, for a word. Some stayed and built huts nearby.
Athanasius says the desert became like a city, filled with monks.

A monk is someone who leaves ordinary life to live for God in prayer, alone or with others. Catholic monks and nuns still do, in monasteries around the world. Tradition calls Anthony the father of monks.

how: Catholic monks and nuns live under vows in monasteries, praying together through the day, and the Church keeps the feast of Saint Anthony the Abbot each year.

games.q: you're Anthony. you walk into church and hear: if thou wilt be perfect, go sell what thou hast, and give to the poor. what do you do?
o: go away sad, like the young man in the Gospel.
give the land away and sell the rest for the poor.
give a little and keep the land.
games.why: Athanasius says Anthony gave his land to his village and sold the rest for the poor, doing what the young man in the Gospel couldn't.

practice: Nobody is asking you to sell the house. Let your mind find one thing at home you don't need that someone else could use, a coat, a book, and notice whether there's a small tug of wanting to keep it.
If there is, that tug is where Anthony's story lives; if you pray, offer the thing, and the tug, to God.
